In mathematical [[set theory]], '''Chang's model''' is the smallest [[inner model]] of set theory closed under [[countable set|countable]] sequences. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Chang|year=1971|authorlink=Chen Chung Chang}}. More generally Chang introduced the smallest inner model closed under taking sequences of length less than κ for any infinite [[Cardinal number|cardinal]] κ. For κ countable this is the [[constructible universe]], and for κ the first uncountable cardinal it is Chang's model.

Chang's model is a model of [[Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory|ZF]]. [[Kenneth Kunen]] proved in {{harvs|txt|last=Kunen|year=1973|authorlink=Kenneth Kunen}} that the [[axiom of choice]] fails in Chang's model provided there are sufficient large cardinals, such as uncountably many [[measurable cardinal]]s.
